chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Dawud ibn Sirhan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
There is no Itikaf (spiritual retreat) except during the last ten days of the month of Ramadan.

And he said: Indeed Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: 'I do not consider Itikaf to be valid except in the Sacred Mosque (Al-Masjid Al-Haram), or the Mosque of the Messenger (Al-Masjid Al-Nabawi), or a congregational Mosque (Al-Masjid Al-Jami').
And it is not befitting for the person performing Itikaf to leave the mosque except for a necessity that is required, and then he should not sit [outside] until he returns.
And the woman is similar to that [in ruling].

key_terms.الاعْتِكَاف: Itikaf: Spiritual retreat in a mosque
key_terms.الْعِشْرِينَ: The last ten days (literally: the twentieth)
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ الرَّسُولِ: The Mosque of the Prophet (in Medina)

ai.seo_question: What are the valid locations and conditions for Itikaf in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the preferred location for Itikaf, citing Imam al-Sadiq’s restriction to the last twenty days of Ramadan and Imam Ali’s preference for the three holiest mosques (Mecca, Medina, and Kufa). It further clarifies the juristic condition that a mutakif must not remain outside the mosque for non-essential matters, ensuring the continuity of spiritual immersion, a rule applied equally to men and women.

en.hubeali:
Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Dawood Bin Sirham, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
There is no Itikaaf except during the twentieth of a Month of Ramazan’.
And heasws said: ‘Aliasws was saying: ‘Iasws do not view the Itikaaf (as correct) except in the Sacred Masjid, or Masjid of the Rasoolsaww, or a general Masjid.
And, it is not befitting for the performer of Itikaaf that he goes out from the Masjid except for a need which is a must from it. Then he should not sit until he returns.
And (for) the woman, is similar to that’.
en.sarwar: 2. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Dawud ibn Sarhan who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Without passing the twentieth day of the month of Ramadan Ttikaf is not valid.’
He (the Imam) then said that Ali ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would say, “I do not see Ttikaf, unless it is in Masjid al-Haram, Masjid of the Messenger of Allah, or a Jami‘ Masjid (central).
It is not proper for one performing ’Ttikaf to go out of Masjid except for one’s urgent needs without which one cannot do, but then one must not sit down until one returns.
The same rule applies to women.’””
